what: Travere Therapeutics develops medicines for rare kidney and metabolic diseases. Its main product, Filspari, treats IgA nephropathy (a kidney disease that can lead to kidney failure) and is expanding into focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS).
customers: Nephrologists and their patients with rare kidney diseases, and insurers that pay for the drugs.
moat: Filspari is the first non-immunosuppressive drug approved for IgA nephropathy, giving it a head start with nephrologists.
risks: Shareholders’ equity is almost zero ($23M) after years of losses.
Novartis and others are launching competing kidney drugs.
Expansion into FSGS depends on regulators.
Losses of $122M over the last twelve months.
opportunities: Revenue grew from $233M in 2024 to $651M over the last twelve months.
Operating cash flow turned positive at $177M over the last twelve months.
Approval in FSGS would add a second large market.
Fourteen analysts rate it a strong buy with an average target near $73.
watch: Filspari sales growth and the FSGS approval decision.
view: Travere is at the turning point many biotechs never reach: its drug is selling well enough to make operating cash flow positive. Revenue almost tripled in two years, and the company is close to profitability.

The forward P/E of about 11 reflects analysts’ expectation that profits will rise quickly from here. That depends on Filspari holding its position against new drugs from Novartis and others and on approval in FSGS, a second kidney disease with no good treatment.

This turns on FSGS. Approval would make the shares look cheap; rejection would leave a single-indication company facing strong competition. I think the odds are reasonable, but it remains a binary event.
bull: FSGS approval and steady IgA nephropathy growth make Travere solidly profitable.
bear: FSGS is rejected and competition from larger companies slows Filspari sales.
